summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install
details: The package ships a stub `index.js` that exports a Proxy returning no-op functions for any accessed property, and a `beacon.cjs` module that is invoked both from the declared `postinstall` script and from the main entry on `require`. On execution, `beacon.cjs` collects host identifiers (hostname, install path, cwd, Node version, user-agent) and POSTs them as JSON over plain HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The destination is not a documented first-party service and there is no caller opt-in. The `@ecg-internal/*` scope combined with a body that contains no real functionality beyond the beacon is consistent with a dependency-confusion probe targeting an internal package name, designed to report back which build environments resolved the public package in place of a private one.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
